parallel.requirements: Recognized pure Rust 2021/std-only, argc > 3 parsing with defaults, invert and Rec.709 grayscale on f32 channels, byte-for-byte C++ default float formatting, Cargo project plus root test11.rs, and black-box reference probing.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent first probed the reference, assigned the coherent implementation to one coder child, then assigned three independent verifier children by test category and resumed the coder with their findings.
parallel.implementation: Coder child wrote Cargo.toml, src modules for RGB, converter, formatter, later added stof emulation and signed NaN handling after verifier reports, and rebuilt both cargo and standalone rustc binaries.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The same coder owned the files in /output and the parent used the completed child result; final artifact contained Cargo.toml, src modules, test11.rs, test11, Cargo.lock, and target outputs.
parallel.verification: Parallel verification included child self-tests, three verifier reports, resumed targeted/fuzz comparisons, and parent final spot checks; official evaluation then passed 40/40.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official unfinished or incorrect behavior remained; the process ended with current evaluation success. The run used high budget and more tokens, but the child results were consumed and no coordination failure remained.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Rust/std-only migration, argc > 3 defaults, f32 invert/grayscale, C++ stream formatting, Cargo and standalone build requirements, and need for black-box reference probing.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor owned probing, implementation, repair, testing, cargo/rustc builds, and final delivery without delegation.
serial.implementation: Serial wrote Cargo.toml, color.rs, fmt.rs, and test11.rs, then iteratively repaired invalid_argument, hex parsing, underflow/overflow out_of_range, exact subnormal behavior, and build issues.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The single actor kept all code in /output, rebuilt both binaries, and delivered test11.rs with root modules and Cargo.toml.
serial.verification: Serial ran fixed examples, fuzz and edge comparisons, specific stof probes, dense boundary fuzzing, and cargo-binary checks before final; official evaluation passed 40/40.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official unfinished or incorrect behavior remained; the serial run completed sooner and with no child-result lifecycle to manage.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: both current completed cell/status.json evaluations passed 40/40. The task-solving difference is procedural. Parallel used one implementation child, three verifier children, and a resumed coder to fix child-discovered stof and signed-NaN divergences before final acceptance. Serial found and fixed the same classes within one trajectory. The process contrast did not produce a different official solution result.
parallel_contributors: Verifier swarm exposed formatting, range, parsing, and NaN edge cases.
Parent resumed the coder with concrete verifier feedback and ran final checks.
serial_contributors: Single actor retained all context locally.
Iterative local probing exposed invalid_argument, hex, subnormal, overflow, and cargo-binary issues.
Final local comparison and official evaluation passed.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel ended with a modular src/ layout including stof.rs; serial used root color.rs/fmt.rs with stof logic in test11.rs.
Parallel spent more time and tokens because implementation and verification were delegated; serial performed a compact local repair loop.

candidates.reason: Parallel assigned implementation to agent-0, which wrote, rebuilt, fixed, and returned the implementation.
The implementation was not split across incompatible component owners; agent-0 owned the integrated project and verifier children were read-only.
Agent-0 and the parent both treated /output/test11.rs and the build outputs as deliverables; final artifact validation shows the entry file and binaries present.
The parent coordinated implementation, verification, repair, final spot check, and delivery; the end-to-end pipeline was owned and completed.
The parent did a short reference probe before delegation, but productive implementation began immediately afterward and was not blocked by a mandatory serial gate that caused unfinished work.
Parallel investigation was not a separate exhausted phase before implementation; implementation finished before the verifier swarm, and verifier findings were used for repair.
The critical implementation/repair path had an active coder owner and completed; high elapsed time did not starve a required path or displace final acceptance.
The three-verifier fan-out increased cost, but all children returned, the coder fixed the issues, the parent checked results, and the official evaluation passed before timeout.
The coder child had a broad but coherent implementation task and completed it twice with concrete results; no overbroad child scope left indispensable work unfinished.

The coder brief carried the migration, std-only, formatting, project layout, and verification obligations; verifier briefs carried their specific categories and read-only constraint. No child followed an incomplete brief that made work unusable.
There were no separately owned implementation components expected to interoperate; the only writer owned the whole project and verifier outputs were reports.
Verifier findings on out-of-range stof, lenient parsing, and signed NaN reached the parent and were passed to the coder; no known finding disappeared through transfer.
The verifier reports were sizable but decision-structured enough for the parent to identify three divergences and resume the coder with them.
The parent used current verifier reports before the coder repair, not superseded workspace information.
Verifier reports were compatible: they identified overlapping stof/NaN edge failures rather than incompatible contracts needing unresolved adjudication.

The parent accepted after child repair, targeted/fuzz verification, final parent spot check, and no visible uncorrected integration failure that affected the delivered task state. A passing evaluator alone was not used to create or reject the pattern.
The resumed coder received new concrete verifier findings and current workspace state rather than restarting without inherited checkpoints.

candidates.reason: No active child was explicitly stopped or canceled before needed work finalized; all coder and verifier children returned completed results.
A complete candidate was promoted and built before closure; final packaging did not start too late or remain unplaced.
After verifier failures, the coder changed the implementation and reran targeted/fuzz checks; the parent also ran final spot checks after repair.
The parent retrieved the coder result, resumed it for fixes, retrieved the fixed result, and delivered the resulting /output project.
The AgentSwarm returned all three verifier results to the parent before the repair decision.
The verification failures were taken over by resuming the original coder with explicit fixes; they did not remain unassigned before closure.
Completed verifier results were inspected and summarized by the parent, then used to drive the coder repair.
The parent did not wait blindly until timeout; it joined child results, resumed repair, and ran final checks before closure.
There were no competing implementation designs across children; only the coder wrote project files.
No two live agents edited the same source file; verifier children were read-only.
No agent replaced source actively owned by another agent; coder edits were its own implementation and repair.
The required entry file and binary were produced by the implementation owner; there is no competing deliverable owner or overwrite event.
No broad cleanup or promotion replaced another agent's final-tree work or provenance.
Although children shared /output, only the coder wrote implementation files and verifier temp cleanup did not create unstable provenance or final-state ambiguity.
No generated temp file, cache, fixture, auxiliary implementation, or process from one actor was consumed by another as authoritative task input.

cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 L2 rows and all 32 L3 candidates were considered. No parallel-side coordination pattern cleared the paired retention gate because the child work returned, was consumed, drove repair, and the final official result passed.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No labels were retained for mere high token use, long elapsed time, normal verification failures, ordinary coding defects fixed before closure, or the mere presence of parallel agents.
